courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Elementary Wolof I
courses.description: Introduction to Wolof; emphasizes grammar, pronunciation, reading, and conversation in standard Wolof. Same as AFST 241. Participation in language laboratory required.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Elementary Wolof II
courses.description: Continuation of elementary Wolof, with introduction of more advanced grammar; emphasizes more fluency in speaking, reading, and writing simple sentences in standard Wolof. Same as AFST 242.
courses.prereqText: WLOF 201. Participation in language laboratory required.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Intermediate Wolof I
courses.description: Survey of more advanced grammar, with emphasis on increasing conversational fluency, composition skills, study of written texts in standard and Dakar Wolof, and discussion of grammatical variations. Same as AFST 443. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Intermediate Wolof II
courses.description: Continuation of WLOF 403. Emphasizes ability to engage in reasonably fluent discourse in Wolof, comprehensive knowledge of formal grammar, and ability to read ordinary texts in standard and Dakar Wolof. Same as AFST 444. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Advanced Wolof I
courses.description: Third year Wolof with emphasis on conversational fluency and on increased ability in reading and comprehending texts, including newspaper prose and West African cultural materials. Course will also deal with the advanced level grammar found in such texts. Same as AFST 445. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Advanced Wolof II
courses.description: Continuation of WLOF 405 with increased emphasis on conversational fluency and comprehension of advanced level grammar in the reading of a variety of prose tests on current cultural issues. Same as AFST 446. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: WLOF
courses.title: Topics Wolof Lang & Lit I
courses.description: Selected readings from modern Wolof authors, with a focus on novels, plays, and basic poetry illustrative of West African cultural issues and advanced level Wolof grammar, as well as development of expository writing skills. Same as AFST 447. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
